claim: The Step6C uncertainty method is a fixed, track-level cross-fit conformal procedure using a trackwise maximum canonical Euclidean error score; TestReal and Fresh evaluations reuse the locked q values without post-test recalibration.
basis: R4B protocol lock and exact q provenance.

claim: At the 2-second horizon, fixed conformal prediction regions are conservative on both TestReal and Fresh WildBox.
basis: Both 90% and 95% window-level coverages exceed targets on both datasets.

claim: At the 5-second horizon on TestReal, fixed conformal coverage remains above nominal targets, but this evidence is retrospective rather than a pristine confirmatory uncertainty test.
basis: TestReal 5s window coverage is 94.07% for 90% target and 98.06% for 95% target; dataset role is RETROSPECTIVE_AFTER_STEP6A_6B.

claim: Fresh WildBox 5-second q90 transfer under-covers, especially at the track-macro level, so long-horizon 90% uncertainty transfer is not reliably calibrated across domain.
basis: Fresh 5s q90 window coverage is 86.03% and track-macro coverage is 79.17% versus a 90% target.

claim: Fresh WildBox 5-second q95 transfer is closer to nominal coverage than q90, but does not justify a claim of perfect calibration.
basis: Window coverage is 93.56% versus 95% target while track-macro coverage is 95.50%; Fresh is diagnostic-only/already inspected.

claim: The fixed conformal uncertainty method is calibrated at 90% and 95% across all horizons and datasets.
basis: Fresh WildBox 5s q90 materially under-covers and q95 is mixed.

claim: Fresh WildBox provides pristine confirmatory uncertainty validation.
BIRDSAI TestReal provides a pristine untouched uncertainty holdout.
The uncertainty results support a horizon-dependent transfer story: short-horizon uncertainty is conservative, whereas long-horizon cross-domain calibration degrades.
basis: 2s coverage is consistently above nominal; Fresh 5s q90 under-covers.
